title: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach
author: Stuart Russell, Peter Norvig
summary: The definitive comprehensive introduction to the theory and practice of artificial intelligence. Covers intelligent agents, uninformed and heuristic search, adversarial search, constraint satisfaction, knowledge representation, probabilistic reasoning, machine learning, deep learning, reinforcement learning, and AI ethics and safety.
table_of_contents: 8. Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
10. Philosophy, Ethics, and the Future of AI

citations.apa: Russell, S., & Norvig, P. (2020). Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach (4th ed.). Pearson.
citations.mla: Russell, Stuart, and Peter Norvig. Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach. 4th ed., Pearson, 2020.
citations.ieee: S. Russell and P. Norvig, Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach, 4th ed. Pearson, 2020.

sample_chunks: An intelligent agent is anything that can be viewed as perceiving its environment through sensors and acting upon that environment through actuators.
A rational agent is one that acts so as to achieve the best outcome or, when there is uncertainty, the best expected outcome.
The A* search algorithm evaluates nodes by combining g(n), the cost to reach the node, and h(n), the estimated cost to get from the node to the goal: f(n) = g(n) + h(n).

title: Introduction to Algorithms
author: Thomas H. Cormen, Charles E. Leiserson, Ronald L. Rivest, Clifford Stein
summary: Universally recognized as the bible of algorithms (CLRS). Provides in-depth theoretical analysis and practical pseudocode for fundamental data structures, divide-and-conquer algorithms, dynamic programming, greedy algorithms, graph traversal (Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford), maximum flow, and NP-completeness.
table_of_contents: 1. The Role of Algorithms in Computing
5. Data Structures: Red-Black Trees, Hash Tables, Heaps
6. Advanced Design: Dynamic Programming and Greedy Algorithms
7. Graph Algorithms: BFS, DFS, MST, Shortest Paths

citations.ieee: T. H. Cormen, C. E. Leiserson, R. L. Rivest, and C. Stein, Introduction to Algorithms, 4th ed. MIT Press, 2022.

sample_chunks: An algorithm is any well-defined computational procedure that takes some value, or set of values, as input and produces some value, or set of values, as output.
Dynamic programming solves problems by combining the solutions to subproblems, storing results to avoid recalculating the same subproblem multiple times.
Dijkstra's algorithm solves the single-source shortest-paths problem on a weighted, directed graph G = (V, E) for the case in which all edge weights are nonnegative.

title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
author: Martin Kleppmann
summary: An industry milestone exploration of data system architecture. Deep dives into storage engines (LSM-trees vs B-trees), data encoding, replication strategies (single-leader, multi-leader, leaderless), partitioning, transactions (ACID, isolation levels, serializability), and distributed consensus (Raft, Paxos).
table_of_contents: 8. The Trouble with Distributed Systems (Clocks, Split-brain)

citations.apa: Kleppmann, M. (2017). Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems. O'Reilly Media.
citations.mla: Kleppmann, Martin. Designing Data-Intensive Applications. O'Reilly Media, 2017.
citations.ieee: M. Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications. O'Reilly Media, 2017.

sample_chunks: Reliability means continuing to work correctly even when things go wrong (tolerating hardware or software faults, and human error).
A storage engine based on Log-Structured Merge-Trees (LSM-trees) appends all writes sequentially to a memtable, then flushes immutable SSTables to disk with background compaction.
Linearizability is a recency guarantee: once a read sees a new write, all subsequent reads must see that value or an even newer one.

title: Deep Learning
author: Ian Goodfellow, Yoshua Bengio, Aaron Courville
summary: Widely known as the Deep Learning Bible by MIT Press. Covers mathematical foundations (linear algebra, probability, information theory, numerical computation), deep feedforward networks, regularization, optimization, convolutional networks, sequence modeling, and generative adversarial networks (GANs).
table_of_contents: 1. Applied Math and Machine Learning Basics
6. Sequence Modeling: Recurrent and Recursive Nets
key_concepts: Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) with Momentum and Adam

citations.apa: Goodfellow, I., Bengio, Y., & Courville, A. (2016). Deep Learning. MIT Press.
citations.mla: Goodfellow, Ian, Yoshua Bengio, and Aaron Courville. Deep Learning. MIT Press, 2016.
citations.ieee: I. Goodfellow, Y. Bengio, and A. Courville, Deep Learning. MIT Press, 2016.

sample_chunks: Deep learning is a specific subfield of machine learning: a new take on learning representations from data that puts an emphasis on learning successive layers of increasingly meaningful representations.
The backpropagation algorithm allows information from the cost to flow backward through the network in order to compute the gradient with respect to every parameter.
Generative Adversarial Networks set up a minimax game between two networks: a generator that manufactures fake data and a discriminator that detects fakes.

title: Quantum Computation and Quantum Information
author: Michael A. Nielsen, Isaac L. Chuang
summary: Known affectionately as 'Mike and Ike', this is the definitive standard textbook on quantum computing. Explains quantum mechanics foundations, qubits, quantum teleportation, quantum circuits, Shor's factoring algorithm, Grover's quantum search, quantum error correction, and physical implementations of quantum computers.
table_of_contents: 3. Quantum Circuits and Universal Gate Sets
4. Quantum Fourier Transform and Shor's Algorithm
key_concepts: Grover's Quadratic Speedup for Unsorted Search

citations.apa: Nielsen, M. A., & Chuang, I. L. (2010). Quantum Computation and Quantum Information (10th anniversary ed.). Cambridge University Press.
citations.mla: Nielsen, Michael A., and Isaac L. Chuang. Quantum Computation and Quantum Information. Cambridge UP, 2010.
citations.ieee: M. A. Nielsen and I. L. Chuang, Quantum Computation and Quantum Information, 10th anniversary ed. Cambridge University Press, 2010.

sample_chunks: A qubit is a two-state quantum-mechanical system, such as the polarization of a single photon, capable of existing in arbitrary linear superpositions of |0> and |1>.
Quantum entanglement occurs when pairs or groups of particles cannot be described independently of the state of the others, even when separated by large distances.
Shor's algorithm can factor an integer N in polynomial time O((log N)^3), breaking RSA cryptography on a sufficiently large fault-tolerant quantum machine.

title: Gödel, Escher, Bach: An Eternal Golden Braid
author: Douglas R. Hofstadter
summary: Pulitzer Prize winning tour de force exploring the emergence of consciousness and cognition through self-reference, formal axiomatic systems, recursive patterns in Johann Sebastian Bach's fugues, M.C. Escher's impossible woodcuts, and Kurt Gödel's Incompleteness Theorems.
table_of_contents: 3. Figure and Ground in Art and Logic
7. The Propositional Calculus & Typographical Number Theory
8. Gödel's Theorem: Strange Loops and Tangled Hierarchies
key_concepts: Gödel's First and Second Incompleteness Theorems
Isomorphism and Syntactic vs Semantic Meaning

citations.mla: Hofstadter, Douglas R. Gödel, Escher, Bach: An Eternal Golden Braid. Basic Books, 1999.
citations.ieee: D. R. Hofstadter, Gödel, Escher, Bach: An Eternal Golden Braid. Basic Books, 1999.

sample_chunks: The 'Strange Loop' phenomenon occurs whenever, by moving upwards or downwards through the levels of some hierarchical system, we unexpectedly find ourselves right back where we started.
Gödel showed that any consistent formal system capable of expressing elementary arithmetic contains propositions that are true but unprovable within the system itself.
Can machines think? Hofstadter suggests minds are emergent phenomena arising from intricate strange loops of symbolic self-representation within our neural substrate.

title: Brave New World
author: Aldous Huxley
summary: A chilling prophecy of a technologically controlled World State where human reproduction is industrialized via the Bokanovsky Process, psychological conditioning replaces freedom, and synthetic pleasure (soma) eliminates dissatisfaction, confronting the tragic outsider John the Savage.
table_of_contents: 1. The Central London Hatchery and Conditioning Centre
3. The Mechanism of the World State
6. John the Savage's Encounter with Civilization
key_concepts: Soma as the Instrument of Voluntary Enslavement
Loss of Art, Truth, and Tragedy in Exchange for Comfort

citations.mla: Huxley, Aldous. Brave New World. Chatto & Windus, 1932.
citations.ieee: A. Huxley, Brave New World. Chatto & Windus, 1932.

sample_chunks: Community, Identity, Stability—such was the World State's motto.

A really efficient totalitarian state would be one in which the all-powerful executive of political bosses and their army of managers control a population of slaves who do not have to be coerced, because they love their servitude.
'Actual happiness always looks pretty squalid in comparison with the overcompensations for misery... stability isn't nearly so spectacular as instability.'

title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
author: Daniel Kahneman
summary: Nobel Laureate Daniel Kahneman's masterpiece detailing the two modes of thought that drive the human mind: System 1 (fast, instinctive, emotional, prone to systematic cognitive illusions) and System 2 (slow, deliberative, logical, but mentally lazy). Covers loss aversion, framing effects, and prospect theory.
table_of_contents: 2. Heuristics and Biases: Anchoring, Availability, Representativeness
3. Overconfidence and the Illusion of Validity
4. Choices: Prospect Theory and Loss Aversion
5. Two Selves: The Experiencing Self vs Remembering Self
key_concepts: Prospect Theory and Loss Aversion (losses hurt 2x more than gains feel good)
WYSIATI (What You See Is All There Is)

citations.apa: Kahneman, D. (2011). Thinking, Fast and Slow. Farrar, Straus and Giroux.
citations.mla: Kahneman, Daniel. Thinking, Fast and Slow. Farrar, Straus and Giroux, 2011.
citations.ieee: D. Kahneman, Thinking, Fast and Slow. Farrar, Straus and Giroux, 2011.

sample_chunks: System 1 operates automatically and quickly, with little or no effort and no sense of voluntary control.
System 2 allocates attention to the effortful mental operations that demand it, including complex computations.
The confidence people have in their beliefs is not a measure of the quality of evidence, but of the coherence of the story that the mind has managed to construct.

title: Clean Code: A Handbook of Agile Software Craftsmanship
author: Robert C. Martin
summary: Classic guide to crafting readable, maintainable software. Covers meaningful naming, function design (doing one thing well), comments as failures to express intention, formatting, error handling, unit testing (FIRST principles), and object-oriented SOLID principles.
table_of_contents: 2. Functions: Small and Doing One Thing
6. Error Handling: Use Exceptions Rather than Return Codes
key_concepts: The Boy Scout Rule: Leave the campground cleaner than you found it
Functions should do one thing, do it well, and do it only
FIRST Unit Test Principles (Fast, Independent, Repeatable, Self-validating, Timely)

citations.apa: Martin, R. C. (2008). Clean Code: A Handbook of Agile Software Craftsmanship. Prentice Hall.
citations.mla: Martin, Robert C. Clean Code: A Handbook of Agile Software Craftsmanship. Prentice Hall, 2008.
citations.ieee: R. C. Martin, Clean Code: A Handbook of Agile Software Craftsmanship. Prentice Hall, 2008.

sample_chunks: Clean code is not written by following a set of rules; it is developed through the acquisition of craftsmanship and care.
Any fool can write code that a computer can understand. Good programmers write code that humans can understand.
The ratio of time spent reading versus writing code is well over 10 to 1. Making code easy to read actually makes it easier to write.

title: Molecular Biology of the Cell
author: Bruce Alberts, Rebecca Heald, Alexander Johnson, David Morgan
summary: The gold standard textbook of cell biology. Details cell structure, genome maintenance, DNA replication and repair, transcription and translation, membrane transport, cell signaling cascades, cytoskeleton dynamics, cell cycle regulation, apoptosis, and stem cell biology.
table_of_contents: 6. From DNA to RNA to Protein
7. Control of Gene Expression and Epigenetics

sample_chunks: All living cells on Earth store their hereditary information in the form of double-stranded DNA molecules.
Cells replicate their genetic information by template-directed polymerisation, copying the nucleotide sequences with extraordinary fidelity.
Signal transduction pathways convert extracellular stimuli into specific intracellular responses through cascades of phosphorylation and secondary messengers.
